claims.text: The ledger is the sole entry point downstream.** Every element of the generated matrix and the map traces to a ledger entry id, and no matrix cell or map element exists whose content came from anywhere else.

claims.text: Intake is schema-pinned and validated.** Every line of `glossa-indus/ledger/claims.jsonl` validates against the pinned ledger schema (`ledger-schema v1`), and the Stage 1 validator, run in CI, rejects a malformed, extra-field, or missing-field entry.

falsification_tests: two canonical entries with one fingerprint; an entry whose stored fingerprint differs from recomputation; or a seeded duplicate intake that is written.
claims.text: D-B dedupe is enforced at intake, not by memory.** Every canonical entry's `proposition_fingerprint` recomputes to its stored value under the frozen rules (`spec029-phase-i-v1`), no two canonical entries share a fingerprint, and an intake attempt whose fingerprint collides with an existing proposition is refused, naming both records, writing nothing.

claims.text: Corrections are append-only reclassifications.** A superseded claim is marked by an appended reclassification entry with a `supersedes` pointer; no existing ledger line is ever edited in place.

claims.text: No field is fabricated at migration or intake.** A migrated or intaken entry carries a `falsifier` or a `does_not_establish` line only where its source record carries one or a named human-authored record supplies one; where neither exists the field is null, and every gate run publishes the falsifier-coverage count of the ledger.

claims.text: OD-2 authorship is preserved.** No ledger entry carries explanation content (`explanation_record`, or a `does_not_establish` line sourced from one) unless it names a human author whose adoption act exists in a durable record; the intake validator rejects explanation content without one.

claims.text: The matrix is generated, never made.** `glossa-indus/matrix/matrix.json` and `matrix.md` are produced solely by the registered generator from the ledger; deleting them and regenerating from an unchanged ledger reproduces them byte-for-byte.

claims.text: Every matrix cell is traceable to its derivation.** Every non-empty cell names its relation, its citation ids, and the registered derivation rule (matrix-defs version) that produced it, and inspecting the cited ledger entries exhibits that rule's stored relation.

falsification_tests: a seeded Atlas-style miscarriage — a citation that exists and is relevant but satisfies no tie rule (e.g., citing Spec 054's UNEXECUTED closure as support for the Yadav claim) — that the gate passes; or any production cell/edge citation the gate's V4 check cannot tie.
claims.text: Citations carry their relations (adopted, Atlas note 2026-11-01).** For every citation on every non-empty matrix cell and every map edge, at least one registered tie mechanically holds (spec.md Point 4: T1 source membership, T2 dated test with matching outcome direction, T3 registered anchor, T4 registered instrument). Existence, shared documents, shared signs without a T3 anchor record, and topical relevance are not ties.

falsification_tests: a seeded divergence in any one class (a flipped ledger status not reflected in the matrix; a count mismatch; a hand-edited generated artifact) that merges with the job green.
claims.text: The verification gate guards the chain in CI.** A CI job beside C4 (`ledger-gate`) recomputes the matrix and the map from the ledger on every PR and push, running check classes V1–V9 (spec.md Point 4), and a divergence in any class fails the job.

falsification_tests: a negative-control run (seeded divergence) after which the published artifact differs by even one byte from its pre-run hash, or after which the build reports success.
claims.text: Publication is gated (adopted, Atlas note 2026-11-01).** Generated artifacts are published only through candidate → gate → replace: the builder writes a candidate, the gate runs against the candidate, and the published file is replaced only on ALL PASS; on a red gate the previously published artifact is byte-untouched and the build fails.

falsification_tests: a `--regen` run whose byte diff goes unreported, or a downstream defect closed by hand-editing a generated artifact anywhere in the repo's history after this spec lands.
claims.text: Lossless regeneration is a checked mode (adopted, Atlas note 2026-11-01).** The gate's `--regen` mode hashes the matrix and map artifacts, regenerates both from the ledger, and byte-compares; any diff is classified in the run record as exactly the intended change (named) or a downstream defect (fixed by regeneration, never by editing the artifact).
